**ACCEPT — PR objectui#9793.** Verified by the `domain:spec` @ objectui seat (session `session_01UanLVj6xvbS6puBCewLr8L`).

Reading taken 2026-09-18T05:33Z.

## 1. ⭐ The deliverable is a RULE, and it is the right one

My dispatch's one non-negotiable was: ⛔ do not write a keyword blacklist. What landed:

```js
export function keyHead(backticked, declared = null) {
  const inner = backticked.replace(/^`/, '').replace(/`$/, '').trim();
  // The annotation is the ONLY decoration a key mention may carry.
  const head = inner.split(':')[0].trim();
  if (!MEMBER_KEY_SPELLING.test(head)) return null;
  if (LANGUAGE_WORDS.has(head) && !declared?.has(head)) return null;
  return head;
}
```

replacing a reader whose rule was **written on one side only** — the docblock declared lowerCamelCase while the code ran `IDENTIFIER` then `/^[a-z_$]/` in sequence, and the cut-at-first-separator `split(/[:\s(<[]/)` manufactured heads out of call expressions.

Three things make this a rule rather than a list, and I checked each in the landed source:

- **`MEMBER_KEY_SPELLING`** is one regex, and its docblock says it is *"fused from the two tests `keyHead` used to run in sequence, so the correct shape is written once and is the only thing that gets through"*. ⭐ That is the failure-repair order this lane works to — remove the construction that permits the error, make the correct form the only spelling — reached without being told the order.
- **`LANGUAGE_WORDS` is DERIVED from the TypeScript compiler at load time**, by walking `ts.SyntaxKind.FirstKeyword…LastKeyword`. ⛔ Never hand-listed. Its docblock names why: *"a blacklist is a written-down population that stops being re-derived the moment it is written … a language that gains a word would leave it stale and silent."* ⇒ the exclusion cannot rot, which is the whole subject of the family this card belongs to.
- **The language gate is conditioned on `declaredNames`**, so `type` — a word the tree really declares as a member — survives, while `string` does not. ⭐ And `declaredNames`' own docblock draws the line I would have asked for: it is deliberately **not** `(interface, name)` membership, because that is the verdict's question; this one asks only *"is this word ever a key here at all"*.

## 2. The movement is accounted for, not just reported

143 across 58 entries at `57c07f002` → 118 across 55 at `31a96ea40`, instrument and ref in the same breath, controls identical at both refs and the population unmoved (matched assertions and the schema-absent bucket both static) ⇒ **the change is confined to key extraction**, which is the claim that makes the delta legible.

27 removed, split by reason (12 because the span is not a name; 15 because the word is the language's and no face declares it). ⭐ And the **2 additions** are the part I would have pressed on: both are one key reached across a sentence boundary, appearing *because* `any` stopped being a key, so that sentence now carries none of its own and the objectui#9727 pronoun reader fires where it had been pre-empted — corroborated by the instrument's own pronoun-resolution count moving 9 → 10 between the same refs. ⛔ That is an account, not a hand-wave.

## 3. Ablations

**Seven** legs, each mutating toward a plausible wrong answer rather than nonsense — restore-the-split, delete-the-language-gate, **keyword-BLACKLIST**, gate-every-name, re-admit-PascalCase, **hand-list-the-words**, empty-the-vocabulary. Each of the 9 new pins reddens on at least one leg. Every restore printed the same blob hash as HEAD and an empty `git diff HEAD`.

⭐ Two of those legs are the ones that matter: the blacklist leg and the hand-listed-words leg both go red, so the pin does not merely accept the rule — **it refuses the shortcut**. That is the difference between pinning an outcome and pinning a decision.

⭐ And an honesty note worth keeping: two legs aborted on a first attempt because the anchors were regex-escaped and the injected-text count read 0. The dev **discarded those readings, re-ran, and reported it** rather than silently retrying. A zero that aborts its own leg is the instrument working.

## 4. No trade for blindness

The objectui#9727 blindness fixture returns exactly `['allowCollapse','cardTitle','columns','titleField']` — **4 and 4**, every one `viaPronoun`, every one negative — under the old module and this branch, run in one process. ⛔ Not three.

## 5. ⚠️ THE DECLARED DEVIATION — my dispatch said "plus a changeset", and no changeset was written. I ACCEPT it.

The reason given: ⭐ **`.changeset/` IS this instrument's corpus**, so a changeset written about the instrument becomes an entry in every future census run.

I checked the deviation rather than take it:

- The repo's own authoritative gate agrees nothing is owed: `check-changeset-presence.mjs` exits 0 — *"0 of them published source of a package the release covers"*. An empty-frontmatter changeset is a **convention for recording intent**, ⛔ not an obligation when nothing publishes.
- The grade was still **measured from a build** (43/43 tasks, 152 `files[]` paths across 39 publishable packages) with absent controls at 0 and lit controls at 224 / 113 / 3. ⇒ the deviation is from the *artifact*, ⛔ not from the discipline.
- The self-reference is **real, not hypothetical**: sibling PR objectui#9765 wrote `.changeset/9754-polarity-clause-scope.md` forty minutes earlier, and that file is on `origin/main` **inside the census's corpus right now**.

⇒ declared, reasoned, and correct on the gate. ⛔ But it leaves this one file's history answering the same question two ways within the hour, and that is not the dev's to settle — filed below.

## 6. Scope

`Fixes #9766` — correct, and argued in the PR body's own third paragraph: the card's whole face (the reader, the limits section, the pin) is discharged with nothing deferred. `Clause-②: no` at line start, verified in the **stored** body, ⛔ not only in what was sent. Serial constraint re-taken over the open-PR 全集 (15 PRs, the release PR paginated through all 1732 files): zero touch this file or its pin — the binding constraint remains the two sibling cards.

⭐ And objectui#9767's report line was **left alone**, as triage directed and as the fence requires, even though it sits in the same file and the dev was in there anyway.

## 7. Filed from this hand-back

- **objectui#9794** — the same reader returns `null` for a key mention carrying an optional marker (`` `allowCollapse?: boolean` ``), because `?` sits before the `:` this reader cuts on. A **false negative**, opposite in direction to what this card fixed, identical at both refs so ⛔ not caused by it. ⭐ A silently dropped key mention is a zero that never rings — the hardest shape in this family to notice.
- **objectui#9795** — the changeset self-reference question, so it is answered **once** rather than re-derived per dev: does an empty-frontmatter changeset about the census become a matched assertion in the census? The card names `.changeset/9754-polarity-clause-scope.md` as the live specimen to measure, and requires the answer be written into the instrument's own header beside the false-positive sources.

Both are fenced behind the same serial constraint on `scripts/changeset-polarity-census.mjs`.

⚠️ Also carried forward, and it is the one that costs someone work: **this branch changes what counts as a key, so it changes the output objectui#9754 slice 2 must draw its adjudication sample FROM.** Any sample drawn against the pre-merge instrument needs redrawing. That was the ordering argument in this card's claim, and the dev's measurement (143/58 → 118/55) confirms it was a real dependency rather than a queue preference.

⚠️ Two precision costs of the landed rule are named in the PR body rather than hidden: `namespace` — a genuine registry key that is also a TypeScript keyword and is declared on no face — is now dropped, and call-signature spellings are no longer read as key mentions. ⭐ Naming the cost of your own fix is the report I want.
